text:
maria (runtime): Hey team — can we run a focused onboarding bench for fenrir-2.7b? Need detailed tail-latency sweep + KV-cache warmup behavior. Target hardware: A100-80GB (shared dedicated pool OK). Goals: 50k token sample, seq lengths [512, 2048, 8192], batch sizes [1,4,8], report p50/p95/p99/p999 and mem peak. Also capture async io stalls if any. Can we prioritize this today?

jordan (bench): On it. Do we want native fp16, or try 4-bit int8/4-bit q4 variants too? I'll schedule both but will start with fp16 baseline.

maria (runtime): Start with fp16 baseline first. If stable, then q4_0 and int8 if we have optimized kernels. Make sure KV-cache warmup profile: cold start (single prompt), and steady-state streaming (prefix reuse).

leo (infra): FYI we have a small infra flake on node pool 'gfx-dedicated-2' — ci-bot showed degraded scheduling this morning. Use pool 'gfx-dedicated-1' for strict latency SLO tests. I'll reserve 2 nodes there for the run.

ci-bot: Job queued: bench-job-3942 for fenrir-2.7b (fp16). Allocated on gfx-dedicated-1, 2 nodes. ETA ~18m. Link: https://ci.internal/bench/3942

jordan (bench): Quick note on test harness: I'm running with our standard bench script. Command: ```./bench_run --model=fenfir-2.7b --dtype=fp16 --seqs=512,2048,8192 --batches=1,4,8 --samples=50000 --warmup=200 --metrics=p50,p95,p99,p999,mem,kv_warmup``` Will attach raw artifacts when done.

sam (sre): If you hit 99.9p > 300ms on 512seq we should toggle prefetcher and see if async io is the culprit. Also post the kernel version (Cuda/cuDNN) so we can correlate.

jordan (bench): First pass results (fp16, gfx-dedicated-1): seq=512 b=1 p50=12ms p95=32ms p99=68ms p999=210ms mem_peak=5.2GB; seq=2048 b=1 p50=48ms p95=110ms p99=190ms p999=650ms mem_peak=6.9GB; seq=8192 b=1 p50=180ms p95=420ms p99=810ms p999=2200ms mem_peak=11.8GB. KV warmup shows ~2.3x throughput gain after 3 prompts for long prefix. Raw logs: https://ci.internal/bench/3942/artifacts/logs.tar.gz

maria (runtime): Nice — 999p at 2048 and 8192 look high (650ms / 2200ms). Can you rerun with prefetcher off/on and enable kernel-level tracing? Add `--kernel-trace=light` to the harness.

jordan (bench): Will rerun. Also trying q4_0 next.

ci-bot: Job queued: bench-job-3943 for fenrir-2.7b (fp16, prefetcher=off, kernel-trace=light). ETA ~12m.

jordan (bench): Quick diff from prefetcher toggle (fp16): prefetcher=off reduces p999 at seq=2048 from 650ms -> 510ms, seq=8192 2200ms -> 1750ms. Kernel trace shows occasional memcpy spikes correlated with disk reads at cold starts (first 150 tokens). After warmup those disappear.

leo (infra): That matches known IO window when page cache refills. For streaming-heavy customers we should recommend pinned memory and larger page cache or use the dedicated pool with local NVMe cache.

maria (runtime): Good catch. Jordan — please run q4_0 (quant) on same pool, same sequences, but only 10k samples to save time. Collect quality vs perf sample so we can weigh tradeoff.

jordan (bench): q4_0 10k results (gfx-dedicated-1): seq=512 b=1 p50=10ms p95=28ms p99=55ms p999=180ms mem_peak=3.1GB; seq=2048 p50=40ms p95=95ms p99=165ms p999=520ms mem_peak=4.8GB; seq=8192 p999=1400ms mem_peak=8.6GB. Quality quick-check: token-level perplexity delta ~+0.9% vs fp16 on our evalset. Artifacts: https://ci.internal/bench/3950

sam (sre): Those q4_0 p999 numbers look acceptable for many workloads. Flag: ensure we document the IO warmup behavior in onboarding notes so customers see spike on first few calls.

maria (runtime): Agreed. TL;DR for release notes: fp16 baseline has higher memory but slightly better p999; q4_0 cuts mem by ~40% and improves p999 slightly due to smaller memcpy pressure, quality delta <1%. Action items: 1) Jordan - publish bench brief + artifacts and include kernel/cuda versions. 2) Leo - confirm gfx-dedicated-1 pool reservation for public onboarding tests. 3) Sam - add a note in the onboarding checklist about NVMe pre-warm for long prefix streaming.

jordan (bench): Publishing now: https://wiki.internal/bench/fenrir-2.7b-onboard-1945678901 (contains commands, raw logs, perf CSVs). Posted summary in the bench tracker.

leo (infra): Confirmed reservation for gfx-dedicated-1. I'll add a short runbook for NVMe pre-warm.

sam (sre): I'll draft the onboarding checklist note and link to jordan's artifacts.

maria (runtime): Perfect — thanks everyone. If no regressions in the next 24h we can flip the catalog entry to GA config (default q4_0 + fp16 fallback). :tada:

jordan (bench): Ack, will monitor the CI metrics and reopen if we see anomalies.
